chokepoint.binary_decision: Grant or withhold written approval for temporary emergency potable-water use under the published terms.
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: The temporary-emergency route explicitly requires this office to approve in writing. The other listed exceptions are separate and are not described as requiring that approval.

selected_mechanism.texas_consequence: The proposed campus cooling plan links use of potable city water to local reclaimed-water infrastructure and narrowly specified exceptions.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: The published framework is conditional. Closed-loop cooling describes system design, while the exception language determines when potable water can enter the cooling system. Written permission creates an identifiable local decision record, but does not govern every exception.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Compare the executed text with the published summary, then verify water-delivery deadlines and any emergency approval records before claiming measured water savings or an absolute ban.

evidence_gaps: Executed agreement, adopted amendments and completed annexation were not verified. Analysis is explicitly of the October 2 published terms; KUT separately reports the October 8 approval.
The public summary does not specify the reclaimed-water construction deadline, emergency duration, potable-water volume cap, approval publication process or remedies.
Written City Manager approval is explicit only for the temporary-emergency exception. It must not be inferred for delayed construction or later supply interruption, suspension or shortfall.
No operating water demand, delivered reclaimed-water service, tenant AI workload or completed construction is established. Data-center infrastructure relevance does not identify a tenant.
Direct requests to the two city pages failed TLS negotiation; the web reader recovered the complete readable pages and each was refetched and hashed for final verification.
selected_mechanism.status: October 2 proposed terms verified; October 8 council approval reported by KUT; executed text unverified.
selected_mechanism.independent_trigger_corroboration: KUT independently reports approval after the scheduled October 8 council meeting and describes the water terms. Its fetched full article was inspected.
selected_mechanism.history_comparison: No match among five recent mechanisms. This municipal cooling-water permission is distinct from the earlier statewide TCEQ permit pause.

verified_facts.claim: The City published proposed campus agreement terms on October 2nd, 2026.
Big Watt Digital and PowerHouse Data Centers are the developers of Taylor Technology Campus east of Taylor.
The agreement was scheduled for a Taylor City Council vote on October 8th, 2026.
KUT reports that Taylor council approved the agreement on October 8th, 2026; the report was published October 9th, 2026.
The site would use closed-loop reclaimed-water cooling, with developers funding utility connections.
The published framework identifies a temporary emergency requiring written City Manager approval.
A missed City reclaimed-water construction deadline is a separate exception.
After reclaimed-water service begins, interruption, suspension or reduction below operational requirements is a separate exception.
The city summary describes annexation as bringing the property under city terms; actual annexation completion was not verified.
KUT reports objections from residents regarding the process and describes officials citing increased city oversight.

The primary summary does not supply the construction deadline, potable-water cap or emergency duration. This is a bounded evidence gap, not proof those provisions are absent from the executed agreement.
